question.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given the Value of Their Dot Product
question.problem: Given that $p\cdot q=-5$, find the angle between $p=⟨4t,-2,t⟩$ and $q=⟨1,3,-3⟩.$ Round your answer to $1$ decimal place.
question.worked_solution:
First, since $p\cdot q=-5$, we can solve for $t$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & =-5 \\ 4t\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot 3+t\cdot (-3) & =-5 \\ 4t-6-3t & =-5 \\ t & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨4(1),-2,1⟩ \\  & =⟨4,-2,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $p$ and $q$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{p\cdot q}{|\,p\,||\,q\,|} \\  & =\frac{{p}_{x}{q}_{x}+{p}_{y}{q}_{y}+{p}_{z}{q}_{z}}{\sqrt{{p}_{x}^{2}+{p}_{y}^{2}+{p}_{z}^{2}}\sqrt{{q}_{x}^{2}+{q}_{y}^{2}+{q}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{-5}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}+(-3)^{2}}} \\  & =-\frac{5}{\sqrt{21}\cdot \sqrt{19}} \\  & =-\frac{5}{\sqrt{399}}.\end{aligned}
$$

THerefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(-\frac{5}{\sqrt{399}})≈{104.5}^{∘}.
$$

judgment.reasoning: All 16 mathematical answers agree with their own captured Math Academy worked solutions. The range of arctan is (-\pi/2,\pi/2), giving the selected range values. For both point questions, points I and II satisfy x=tan(y) with y in that interval, while III fails. The complex quotient simplifies to \sqrt{3}/2+\text{i}/2, with magnitude 1 and argument \pi/6. Substitution u=4+x^6 gives the first integral as (4+x^6)^6/18+C; substitution u=x^2+2x gives the second as ln|x^2+2x|+C. Principal inverse trigonometric values give 3\pi/4, 2\pi/3, and -2\pi/3. For the vector questions, cos(theta) equals 19/\sqrt{1961}, 2/\sqrt{754}, 1/\sqrt{182}, -1, -5/\sqrt{399}, and -1/\sqrt{5}, respectively, producing the stated rounded angles. In q-101510, PR=-2PQ, so the angle is exactly 180 degrees. The dot-product constraints give t=1 in q-19038 and t=2 in q-101514. Evidence below comes from worked solutions, not captured grades.
